# Operation coverage

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_ops.py from ops.toml. Do not edit. -->

9 of 11 operations have a kernel. Everything else reaches PyTorch's
CPU implementation through the fallback, which is correct and costs two transfers.

Elementwise operations can share a kernel with their neighbours. Anything else reads
positions it is not writing, so it runs on its own however many kernels it has.

| Operation | ATen | Category | Kernel |
|---|---|---|---|
| `abs` | `aten.abs.default` | elementwise | yes |
| `add` | `aten.add.Tensor`<br>`aten.add.Scalar` | elementwise | yes |
| `div` | `aten.div.Tensor`<br>`aten.div.Scalar` | elementwise | yes |
| `mul` | `aten.mul.Tensor`<br>`aten.mul.Scalar` | elementwise | yes |
| `neg` | `aten.neg.default` | elementwise | yes |
| `relu` | `aten.relu.default` | elementwise | yes |
| `sigmoid` | `aten.sigmoid.default` | elementwise | yes |
| `sqrt` | `aten.sqrt.default` | elementwise | no |
| `sub` | `aten.sub.Tensor`<br>`aten.sub.Scalar` | elementwise | yes |
| `tanh` | `aten.tanh.default` | elementwise | yes |
| `mm` | `aten.mm.default` | matmul | no |

Regenerate with `python tools/gen_ops.py` after editing
[`ops.toml`](../ops.toml).
